chunks.heading: Drone Surveys

chunks.heading: Thermal Imaging

chunks.heading: Electronic Leak Detection

chunks.text: We conduct thorough exterior inspection using drones and direct access where safe. This includes membrane condition, fastener integrity, flashing systems, drainage components, and equipment mounting areas. Every detail is photographed and documented with GPS coordinates. 3

chunks.text: Interior inspection reveals moisture intrusion, insulation performance, and structural conditions. chunks.heading: Step 1: Document the Hail Event
chunks.text: The first step happens immediately after a hail storm. You need to establish that hail occurred at your property: Take photos/videos: Capture any visible damage immediately—dented vents, damaged gutters, hail on the ground Note the date and time: Record when the storm occurred Check local weather reports: Screenshot or save National Weather Service reports showing hail in your area Look for ground markers: Dents in metal mailboxes, AC units, or vehicles help prove hail occurred

chunks.heading: Step 4: Get a Professional Roofing Inspection
chunks.text: This is critical: Before the insurance adjuster visits, have a professional roofing contractor inspect your roof. Here's why: Roofers spot damage adjusters might miss Professional documentation strengthens your claim Having a contractor present during adjuster visit ensures nothing is overlooked Roofers speak the adjuster's language and know what evidence is needed A good roofing contractor will: Conduct a thorough inspection (roof, gutters, vents, flashing) Take detailed photos and measurements Prepare a damage report with aerial drone photography Identify all damaged components (not just obv

chunks.heading: Step 6: Review the Adjuster's Report
chunks.text: After the inspection, you'll receive an adjuster's report and estimate. Review it carefully: Check square footage: Verify it matches your actual roof size Review line items: Ensure all damaged components are included Compare to contractor estimate: Significant differences may indicate issues Look for depreciation: Some policies pay actual cash value (ACV) initially, then depreciation after repairs Verify material quality: Ensure they're approving materials equivalent to what you currently have

chunks.heading: 1. Waiting Too Long to File
chunks.text: While Texas gives you up to 2 years, waiting causes problems: Additional storms make it hard to prove which damage came from which event Minor damage worsens over time (insurance may argue it's now "wear and tear") The sooner you file, the sooner you get your new roof

chunks.heading: 2. Making Temporary Repairs Without Photos
chunks.text: If you make storm repairs (weatherproof sheeting, etc.) before filing, insurance may argue the damage wasn't severe. Always photograph BEFORE making any repairs.

chunks.heading: 4. Accepting the First Offer Without Review
chunks.text: Insurance companies hope you'll accept their initial offer. Don't sign anything until you've had your contractor review it. Once you accept and sign, re-negotiation becomes very difficult.

chunks.heading: 5. Not Documenting Everything
chunks.text: Keep records of: All photos and videos All correspondence with insurance (emails, letters, claim notes) Contractor estimates and reports Weather reports proving hail occurrence Any temporary repair receipts

chunks.heading: Texas "Anti-Steering" Laws
chunks.text: Texas law prohibits insurance companies from: Requiring you to use a specific contractor Penalizing you for choosing your own contractor Paying less if you don't use their "preferred" contractor You have the right to choose your roofing contractor —don't let insurance pressure you otherwise.

chunks.heading: Should I make temporary repairs before filing?
chunks.text: Yes, if there's active leaking—you have a duty to mitigate damage. But photograph EVERYTHING before making repairs. Cover holes with weatherproof sheeting, catch interior drips with buckets, but don't do permanent repairs until the adjuster has inspected. Keep receipts for temporary repairs—these are often reimbursable.

chunks.heading: Insurance Considerations for Amarillo Homeowners
chunks.text: Understanding your insurance coverage is crucial in Amarillo's high-risk weather environment. Most Texas homeowner policies include wind and hail coverage, but the details matter significantly. Deductibles, coverage limits, and claim procedures can vary dramatically between insurers, and many homeowners discover coverage gaps only after suffering storm damage.
